verdict.rationale: Vast.ai exposes real per-hour GPU prices publicly with no account or sales contact: hands-on probes show keyless CLI search and a public REST endpoint returning live offers with per-hour prices, and docs describe a pricing page and a search portal. However, pricing is a host-set marketplace with no fixed rates, so there is no evidenced single published price list per GPU type. Community users also report it takes many clicks to find even an approximate price, which is friction rather than a contradiction. Missing for 10: a documented static public price table covering every GPU type, and a page-level price display confirmed without needing CLI/API queries.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can see the published per-GPU-hour price for every GPU type on a public pricing page without talking to sales

citations.quote: The marketplace model creates natural price competition-hosts compete for your business rather than locking you into fixed rates.
Use `vastai search offers` to query prices programmatically
searched the LIVE GPU marketplace with NO account and NO API key, returning real RTX 4090 offers with CUDA versions, vCPUs, RAM, disk, and per-hour prices
a bare keyless GET to https://console.vast.ai/api/v0/bundles/ returned live marketplace offers as JSON including `dph_total` (per-GPU-hour price)
The search page is the main portal for finding good machines and creating instances on them.
